THE PASSIVE
VOICE
titlePlain: The Passive Voice — The Incident Report (B2)
subtitle: Grammar & Listening · B2 · ~45 min

blocks.title: <ico-recycle></ico-recycle> REPASO EXPRESS · lección anterior
blocks.intro: Antes de empezar, recupera lo de la clase pasada. Une cada expresión con su significado, sin mirar atrás.

blocks.title: <ico-book></ico-book> THE PASSIVE: BE + PARTICIPLE
blocks.intro: Cuando algo sale mal, un profesional cuenta qué pasó y qué se está haciendo, sin señalar a nadie. Para eso sirve la voz pasiva: be + participio.
blocks.note: Cómo funciona: tarjetas , reescribir (aquí escribes tú la frase), completar , escucha , comparar y ordenar . CHECK donde lo veas.

parts.html: 1 · ¿PARA QUÉ? — importa la acción, no quién la hizo

items.sp: Activa: el foco está en Marcos.
Pasiva: el foco está en lo que pasó.

parts.html: 2 · BE + PARTICIPIO — solo cambia «be»; el participio nunca
3 · CUATRO TIEMPOS, UN SOLO VERBO — el tiempo lo marca «be»

items.en: The error was fixed at four.

items.sp: Present perfect: ya está, y es noticia ahora.

items.en: The error is being fixed right now.
The error will be fixed today.

parts.body: is being y has been son las dos que más cuestan. being = está en proceso. been = ya terminó. It is been investigated. → It is being investigated.

parts.html: 4 · ¿CUÁNDO PONER «BY»? — solo si quién lo hizo es noticia

items.en: The prices were updated at 2 a.m.
The site was built by a team of three.
items.sp: Con by: el dato interesante es quién.

parts.html: 5 · UN PASO MÁS: HAVE SOMETHING DONE — otra persona lo hace por ti

items.sp: Hicimos revisar el sistema (lo revisó alguien más).

parts.html: TRAMPA DEL ESPAÑOL — el «se» y dos verbos rebeldes

items.sp: «Se envió el correo ayer»: donde el español usa se, el inglés usa la pasiva.
Happen nunca va en pasiva: a nadie «lo pasan».
«Nací» siempre es pasiva en inglés: was born.

parts.body: It was happened at 2 a.m. → It happened at 2 a.m. · I born in 1995. → I was born in 1995.

blocks.title: <ico-star></ico-star> THE INCIDENT
blocks.intro: A las dos de la mañana, una actualización puso todos los productos de GreenMarket a $0.99. Entraron doscientos pedidos antes de que alguien lo notara. David quiere un nombre; Priya quiere un comunicado.

cast.sp: pasa de la culpa a los hechos

blocks.title: CRISIS WORDS · toca para girar
blocks.intro: El vocabulario de un incidente bien manejado. Aparece en la llamada y en el comunicado.

blocks.title: ACTIVE → PASSIVE
blocks.intro: Reescribe cada frase en voz pasiva: importa qué pasó, no quién lo hizo. Mantén el mismo tiempo verbal.

answers: The file was deleted by someone.

items.source: They updated the prices at 2 a.m.
answers: The prices were updated at 2 a.m.
The prices were updated at 2 am.
The prices were updated at two a.m.
The prices were updated by them at 2 a.m.
The prices were updated at 2 a.m. by them.
At 2 a.m. the prices were updated.
The error has been fixed by us.

items.source: The team is investigating the cause.
answers: The cause is being investigated by the team.

items.source: We will notify every customer today.
answers: Every customer will be notified today.
Every customer will be notified today by us.
Every customer will be notified by us today.
The new prices were not checked.
The new prices were not checked by anybody.
The new prices were not checked by anyone.
The new prices were never checked.
items.why: «Nobody» desaparece y el verbo pasa a negativo: were not checked.

blocks.title: WHICH TENSE OF BE?
blocks.intro: El participio no cambia. Elige la forma de «be» que corresponde al tiempo de la frase.

items.q: The prices ___ updated at 2 a.m. last night.
The error ___ found at four o'clock this morning.
Don't worry. The problem ___ already been fixed.
Two hundred orders ___ placed before anyone noticed.
The process ___ changed since the incident.
We didn't do it ourselves. We ___ the system checked by an expert.

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · THE CRISIS CALL
blocks.desc: David llama furioso y pide un nombre. Priya y Marcos le dan otra cosa: los hechos, en orden.

questions.q: When were the prices updated, and when was the error found?
options: Updated at 2 a.m., found at 4 a.m.
Updated at midnight, found at 2 a.m.

questions.q: What is the situation with the store now?
options: It has been fixed and is back online
The full report will be delivered
All the orders will be canceled

questions.q: Why does Priya avoid naming anyone?
options: She believes the process failed, not one person
She has no idea what happened

speaking.prompt: You are Priya. Give David the four facts again, all in the passive: the update, the discovery, the fix, the next step.
speaking.starter: The prices were (verb) at (time). The error was (verb) at (time). It has been (verb). Every customer will be (verb) today.

transcript.html: Priya, I'm looking at the numbers now. Every product on my site, ninety-nine cents. Two hundred orders! Who did this?
David, I understand you're upset, and you have every right to be. Let me give you the facts first.
I don't want facts. I want a name.
The facts will help you more than a name. Marcos?
The prices were updated at two a.m., in a scheduled update. A file with test prices was uploaded by mistake. The error was found at four, and the store was taken offline right away.
Two hours. Two hundred orders in two hours.
Yes. And here is where we are now. It has been fixed. The correct prices were restored at four thirty, and the store is back online.
And how did a test file get onto my live site?
It is being investigated. You'll have a full report on the root cause by Thursday. I'm not going to guess, and I'm not going to blame one person for a process that failed.
Every customer will be notified today. The email is being written right now.
Fine. Thursday, Priya. I want that report on my desk.

blocks.title: WHO DID IT vs WHAT HAPPENED
blocks.intro: Las dos frases cuentan el mismo hecho. Una apunta a una persona; la otra, a lo que pasó.

items.q: ¿Cuál va mejor en un comunicado público?
¿Qué información tiene A que B no tiene?
El dato interesante es quién construyó el sitio. ¿Qué dices?
options: The site built by Sofia's team.
The site was built by Sofia's team.
The site was build by Sofia's team.

items.q: No sabes quién borró el archivo, y no importa. ¿Qué dices?

blocks.title: BUILD THE PASSIVE
blocks.intro: Toca las palabras en orden. Atención a «is being» y «has been».

items.answer: Every customer will be notified today
The store was taken offline at four

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · THE STATEMENT
blocks.desc: El jueves, Sofia lee el comunicado público de GreenMarket. Fíjate: ni un solo nombre, todo en pasiva.

questions.q: What will happen to the two hundred orders?
options: They will be charged at the full price

questions.q: How will price updates be checked from now on?
options: By two people before they go live

questions.q: Why doesn't the statement say who made the mistake?
options: A public statement is about actions, not blame
The person has left the company

speaking.prompt: Think of a mistake at your work or school. Say three facts about it in the passive, with no names.
speaking.starter: (Something) was (verb) by mistake. The problem was (verb) at (time). It has been (verb).

transcript.html: A statement from GreenMarket. Early on Tuesday morning, incorrect prices were shown on our website for two hours. During that time, two hundred orders were placed at ninety-nine cents per item. The error was found at four a.m., and the correct prices were restored shortly after. All two hundred orders will be honored. No customer will be charged more than the price that was shown. Every affected customer has been notified by email. The cause has been identified, and our update process has been changed. From now on, every price update will be checked by two people before it goes live. We apologize for the confusion, and we thank our customers for their patience.

blocks.title: <ico-pen></ico-pen> THE INCIDENT REPORT
blocks.intro: Escribe el informe de un error real o inventado en tu trabajo (5–7 frases). Sin nombres: solo hechos y próximos pasos.
checklist: Qué pasó y cuándo, en pasiva pasada (was / were + participio)
Qué ya se resolvió (has been + participio)
Qué se está haciendo ahora (is being + participio)
Qué se hará para evitarlo (will be + participio)
by solo si quién lo hizo es un dato importante
blocks.example: On fecha, qué was participio. The problem was found at hora. It has been participio. The cause is being participio. To prevent this, qué will be participio.
blocks.hw: Escribe tu informe y después grábate leyéndolo como un comunicado oficial: despacio y con tono neutral. Envíame texto y audio por WhatsApp.

rubric.d: Escribiste el número de frases que pide la consigna: qué pasó, qué se hizo y qué se hará.
Usaste la pasiva en al menos tres tiempos distintos y bien formada (be + participio).
Un lector lo entiende sin releer: ideas unidas con conectores, sin traducir literal del español.
